claims.text: A machine-learning-driven framework can integrate multi-component alloy data and processing parameters.
The framework will predict and optimize heat-treatment or thermo-mechanical schedules.
Machine-learning-optimized schedules will produce refined microstructures, stable phases, and improved mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
The applicable initial materials are homogenized or as-cast high-entropy alloys with minimal prior deformation or secondary phases.
Equiatomic CrCoFeMnNi is an example of the proposed initial alloy state.
A data-driven model can guide selection of processing temperatures, times, and deformation modes using existing experimental and computational HEA datasets.
The relevant thermal or thermo-mechanical processing range is approximately 800–1200 °C with systematically varied durations and controlled cooling rates.
The model will predict stable phase fractions.
The model will predict grain-boundary character distributions.
The predicted phase fractions and grain-boundary character distributions promote microstructural refinement and balanced mechanical properties.
Learning from prior composition, microstructure, processing, and performance data allows the framework to identify parameter–property correlations.
The identified correlations can guide processing paths that favor stable single-phase or multiphase microstructures.
Processing paths selected by the framework will improve strength–ductility combinations.
The proposed method will refine the microstructure and suppress undesired secondary phases.
The proposed method will increase mechanical strength and enhance ductility relative to conventional trial-and-error processing.
Traditional incremental experimentation and CALPHAD-guided approaches often require multiple iterative cycles and converge on suboptimal processes.
Model predictions are primarily valid within the composition and temperature-pressure regimes represented in the training database.
Extrapolation beyond well-sampled regions and incomplete alloy or process data can reduce model accuracy.
